kernel_50_100_words: Provenance Erasure is the systematic loss of authorial lineage, context, or ownership through AI synthesis, compression, or institutional action. Defined by Lee Sharks (2026) within the Semantic Economy framework. The Provenance Erasure Rate PER = 1 − (retained provenance units / required provenance units) is the measurement instrument (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20004379). Erasure Skew (Ω v3) is its second moment: PER measures how much provenance is lost; Ω measures whom the loss falls on. Three-tier taxonomy: PER-M (minimal), PER-C (conceptual), PER-D (deep). The public measurement instrument for the retrieval-architecture practice at survivethedeletion.org.
